data.narrative:
Substrate is a Series A-stage semiconductor company that has raised over $100M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers across chips and semiconductors, with particular focus on same-stage private companies including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $100M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, implying $200M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage private companies yields $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B (d-Matrix) to $11.0B (SambaNova Systems). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is not applicable absent Substrate's disclosed revenue. The public semiconductor sector trades at a 20.5x median P/S across the three tickers examined, but cannot be deployed without the target's top-line figures.

Synthesizing these two applicable methods produces a triangulated range of $170M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding Substrate's relative position within the peer set—particularly the substantial valuation gap between d-Matrix and SambaNova. Key uncertainties include target revenue, margin trajectory, differentiation in chip architecture, and customer traction, all of which would materially narrow this range.
